## When are goalies pulled?

### Notes before we start:

Important: make conditionings/ definitions on what a golie change is (0651 or 1560 depending on whether its home or not).
pwhl has golie change but not golie pull so NHL is easier to navigate.

Future work: 0641 power play

```{r}

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# Set data directory
data_dir <- "../data/processed/BarDown_cleaned_project"

# Read cleaned datasets
nhl <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "nhl_events_clean.csv"))
pwhl <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "pwhl_events_clean.csv"))
pulls <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "pwhl_candidate_goalie_pulls.csv"))
games <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "pwhl_game_summary.csv"))

# Inspect datasets
glimpse(pwhl)
glimpse(pulls)
glimpse(games)

```

## Visualization 1: When are goalies pulled?

> This visualization shows how many candidate goalie pulls happen at different times in the third period.

```{r}

# Filter third-period goalie pulls
pull_timing <- pulls %>%
  filter(
    period == 3,
    !is.na(pull_time_remaining_sec),
    between(pull_time_remaining_sec, 0, 600)
  ) %>%
  mutate(minutes_remaining = pull_time_remaining_sec / 60)

ggplot(pull_timing, aes(x = minutes_remaining)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10) +
  labs(
    title = "When Do Teams Pull Their Goalies?",
    subtitle = "PWHL candidate goalie pulls in the final 10 minutes",
    x = "Minutes remaining in the third period",
    y = "Number of goalie pulls"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
